name: mcpConnect
description: Connects to a remote MCP server over stdio or HTTP and returns a client handle. The handshake runs at the connect call, so a bad command or URL fails where the developer is looking, rather than at the first tools() call somewhere else. The client declares no capabilities of its own, so it declines a server's sampling or elicitation request rather than leaving the server parked. A tool that reports failure throws an exception (type = "MCPToolError"); a tool with structured output returns that data directly.

params.name: transport
params.description: The transport to use to reach the remote server: "stdio" launches it as a subprocess, "http" talks to it over a URL.

params.name: options
params.description: A struct of transport options. For stdio: command and args. For http: url and headers. Named arguments other than transport are also merged in as options, so both mcpConnect( "stdio", command = "..." ) and mcpConnect( "stdio", { command = "..." } ) work.
